newsitem.title: USA: US Congress in tentative accord on $80 bln funding.
newsitem.headline: US Congress in tentative accord on $80 bln funding.

text.p: A House-Senate conference committee reached tentative agreement Wednesday to provide nearly $80 billion in funding for housing programs, environmental clean-up and veterans' health in fiscal 1997.

While the amount approaches the higher level passed by the Senate, it is still more than $2 billion below the president's request. Several issues relating to housing programs and aerospace research remain to be resolved.

A final accord on the funding hinges on resolution of three politically charged health care issues -- to cover children of veterans with spina bifida, to give new mothers a 48-hour hospital stay option and to expand insurance coverage of mental health treatment.

All three have the strong support of the White House but Republican leaders have suggested the effective date of the three be delayed one year until January 1998 to give more time for review of the proposals.

The Appropriations Committee agreed to President Clinton's demand that the AmeriCorps youth service program be funded in 1996 with $400.5 million. Clinton had threatened a veto of the bill if the House succeeded in killing the program.
As tentatively approved, the bill would provide $5.75 billion for low-income housing. The Environmental Protection Agency's environmental and management programs would receive $1.7 billion.
